A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELVIS research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic and real low-light VIS experiments, VDP-Net ablations, and video-enhancement experiments, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results on the manually annotated ELVIS-S dataset and comparisons against two-stage enhancement-plus-segmentation baselines.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same degradation pipeline, ResNet-18 VDP-Net, temporal fusion, prediction heads, losses and Mask2Former enhancement decoder. Added explanations do not establish changes to training or inference.

E1.justification: v2 adds ELVIS-S, a separately captured collection of five real low-light videos with 250 manually annotated frames. This modestly extends real-video coverage within the existing VIS task; the previous training sources and evaluation datasets remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 introduces a substantial new comparison family: SDSD-Net, StableLLVE and DarkIR enhancement followed by pretrained GenVIS R50. These were not evaluated as VIS comparators in v1. Existing VIS and synthetic-pipeline comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 extends the 100-detection LMOT-S setting already used in v1 Table S2 to the main comparisons and expands AR100 evaluation. New experiments specify enhancement followed by pretrained GenVIS and ELVIS-S evaluation using 50 annotated frames per video cropped to 1080p. Existing training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section S3 and Figure S3 examine false positives and segmentation failures after different enhancement methods, including ELVIS missing a truck. The existing profile-versus-random-sampling comparison gains ELVIS-S evidence. Component ablations, identity-switch examples and histogram-matching analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial real-data results: Table 3 reports ELVIS versus StableLLVE AP of 58.0 versus 57.3 on ELVIS-S and 6.7 versus 3.9 on LMOT-S. Main LMOT-S scores are revised alongside the detection setting, including DVIS++ ViT-L with ELVIS changing from 9.1 to 10.5 AP. GenVIS's 100-detection results already appeared in v1 Table S2; synthetic VIS, component-ablation and enhancement scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same mathematical definitions and objectives. Notation and typesetting refinements do not introduce new assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a claim of beating two-stage baselines by at least 2.8 AP on real low-light videos. The three central contributions and the claimed synthetic-data improvement of up to 3.7 AP remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation that perceptually pleasing enhancement can suppress semantic features needed for VIS. It also replaces v1's noise-dominance and longer-training explanations with arguments about camera-specific ISP generalization and structured degradation sampling. Existing LMOT-S limitations are largely relocated, with a new recommendation to consider both real-video datasets.

D1.justification: v1 promises code upon acceptance; v2 states that code and a dataset are available through a project link. Section S2.1 newly specifies 88 LMOT-S clips of 51 frames, segmentation and category-mapping details, while Section 4.1 describes ELVIS-S capture and annotation. These are disclosures, not evidence that the existing dataset construction changed; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the DarkIR reference and more explicitly positions ELVIS against enhancement-first approaches. It explains excluding Chen et al.'s RAW-output pipeline from evaluation. Most other reference changes are renumbering or capitalization corrections, with the central novelty positioning retained.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, related-work prose and conclusion, reorganizes VIS results into synthetic and real-data subsections, and divides supplementary LMOT-S discussion into construction, results and limitations. These are localized revisions within the retained overall structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3, Table S3 and Figure S3, expands the synthetic-pipeline table with ELVIS-S results, and reformats Tables 1–2 with ELVIS indicators; Table 2 also gains AR100 and backbone grouping. Existing figures and enhancement tables are retained, with some relocation, caption editing and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The manually annotated ELVIS-S evaluation complements v1's reliance on pseudo-labels for real-video VIS, while new two-stage comparisons and clearer construction/access information strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. The gain is limited by ELVIS-S containing only five videos and by an overbroad new abstract claim: Table 3 supports a 2.8 AP margin on LMOT-S, but only 0.7 AP over StableLLVE on ELVIS-S. Overall, the additions provide a useful but bounded improvement.
